messages:
Amy L.: heads-up — on the quickstart sampleapp I got duplicated outgoing webhooks when the SDK retried after a 429 during token refresh. not full-blown repro yet but saw it twice in a row.
Matt K.: ah interesting. is this the node SDK or python?
Amy L.: node. steps: create session -> hit rate limit -> refresh token -> retry. looks like the retry doesn't attach the idempotency key in the retry path.
Sara P.: deploy-bot logged a short spike: deploy-bot: [3309876580] 5xx/429 surge in sandbox-1, correlated with onboarding runs. could paste logs if helpful.
Amy L.: logs would help. I captured the client-side request sequence: initial POST /webhook (429), then POST /auth/refresh (200), then SDK replays original request but without x-idempotency header.
Matt K.: hmm that suggests the retry machinery replays from the auth layer, not the request wrapper which normally sets idempotency. Node code path has a separate retry closure.
Nate R.: I can repro locally in ~5 mins, have a small harness to simulate 429 during refresh. if confirmed we can patch to persist idempotency metadata across the refresh handshake.
Amy L.: thanks! repro script:
```bash
# simulate: token expires, rate-limit main endpoint
node repro/replay_harness.js --mode refresh-429 --concurrency 3
```
outputs: two identical webhook payloads within 200ms.
Matt K.: quick mitigation: set SDK config safeReplayWindow to 0 for onboarding tenants while we patch, and surface warning in quickstart. Not ideal but will prevent duplicate side-effects.
Sara P.: agreed. also thinking we should tweak default jitter: node default is uniform 0-200ms, python is exp backoff with jitter. mismatch makes our platform telemetry noisy.
Amy L.: good point — parity is important for predictable behavior for customers. Nate can we do a patch that (a) copies idempotency header into the retry closure and (b) aligns node jitter to exp+rand?
Nate R.: yeah working on (a) now. (b) needs minor refactor but doable in the same PR. will add unit test that simulates 429 during auth and assert single delivery.
Matt K.: also add a CHANGES entry and a short note in quickstart about idempotency expectations and how to opt out for webhooks.
Amy L.: awesome. once we have PR i'll validate against the sampleapp and push a patch to quickstart. thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: PR #4821 created by nate-r: fix(node): persist idempotency through auth refresh + align backoff jitter. CI run queued.
Sara P.: CI flakiness warning: please include deterministic jitter in test by mocking timers so we don't get random failures.
Nate R.: good call, will use sinon fake timers in tests. will post PR link when green.
Amy L.: perfect — appreciate the quick turnaround. this hits onboarding friction directly so high priority for me.
Matt K.: fyi i'll add a tiny e2e that hits the hosted sandbox endpoint with low rate limit so we catch regression in ci nightly.
Nate R.: sounds good, updating the thread with PR link shortly.
